name: transactions
description: The ledger. Append-only: rows are never updated and never deleted, which is what makes the session's cursor strategy possible (see Architecture.md, Append-only data).

columns.name: previous
columns.description: The preceding transaction of the same account, forming a chain. Unique: no two rows may claim the same predecessor.

columns.name: type_id
columns.note: Only CREATION, SEND and RECEIVE occur here. DECAY and LINK_SUMMARY are virtual — a row carrying them is a bug.

columns.name: balance_gdd4
columns.description: Account balance after this transaction, at balance_date.

columns.name: balance_date
columns.description: The instant balance_gdd4 is valid for. Decay from here forward is computed, not stored.

columns.name: decay_gdd4
columns.description: Decay applied between decay_start and balance_date.

columns.name: decay_calculation_type
columns.description: Which algorithm produced decay_gdd4. Required to reproduce a historical amount — the Decimal.js and fixed-point factors differ in the last unit.

columns.name: creation_date
columns.description: For CREATION rows: the month the contribution was credited for, which is not when it was booked.

columns.name: linked_transaction_id
columns.description: The matching row on the other side: a SEND points at its RECEIVE and back.

columns.name: thank_you_card_id
columns.description: The card this booking was made with, on both rows. The card, not its name — the name is looked up where it is shown.

notes: No created_at, no updated_at, no deleted_at — the row is the event. A correction is a new transaction, never an edit. Both implementations must treat any UPDATE or DELETE on this table as a bug.
Because it is append-only, a session tracks it with a cursor: keep the highest id seen and load only what arrived since. This is the table that strategy exists for.

user_name and linked_user_name are denormalized copies taken at booking time. They are deliberately not refreshed when a user renames — a receipt shows the name as it was. An implementation that joins users to 'correct' them changes history.

open.question: Do the denormalized name and uuid columns survive into gradido2, and at what width?
open.detail: Two varchar(512) names plus four uuids is roughly 100 bytes of struct and up to 1 KiB of payload per row, in the one table the session holds most of. A working set of 200 transactions is dominated by these six columns. Narrowing user_name to the display length actually used, or holding only the ids in the session and resolving names at render time, changes the session budget by an order of magnitude.
open.why_it_matters: This is the single largest term in the fast path's memory footprint. See Architecture.md, Session cache on the fast path.
open.status: unanswered — decide before the transaction domain is rebuilt
